cohort: 395 postpartum women in maternity hospitals within a regional healthcare network in Brazil
finding: Cesarean section rates were higher among multiparous women, women with a history of abortion, and those with an interpartal period of less than 2 years.
mod_finding: Antibiotic therapy and disrespect for childbirth choices were higher among women who underwent cesarean sections, while the use of oxytocin, the presence of a birth companion, and skin-to-skin contact were more common during vaginal deliveries.
